meta.canonicalization: Greek lemmas transliterated and collapsed via headword map (e.g., phantasmata→phantasma; dunamis→dynamis; X/Y compounds split into atoms). Articles (to/hē) stripped.
meta.tier_definition: Tier-A = used by ≥3 of 8 units; Tier-B = used by 1-2 units.

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: motion/change; the genus of phantasia's definition
gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: phantasia as kinesis caused by perception (DA 428b11-15)
gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: De motu causal chain features phantasia as KINETIC mediator. Not González's focus terminologically but conceptually load-bearing.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: Movement; 'energeia is motion' (Rhet. 3.11.1412a.9-10); Kennerly's 'rhetorical kinesis.'
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: In decaying-sense theory: residual perceptual motion persisting in object's absence.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-05: DA 428b/429a: phantasia is a kinēsis caused by sense-perception. Per Newman: 'bringing before the eyes' is a 'lexical form of energeia, a kind of motion realized through the capacity of the mind for seeing things in action.'
gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: motion — phantasia as κίνησις ὑπὸ τῆς αἰσθήσεως κατ' ἐνέργειαν γιγνομένη (DA III.3 428b11-13, 429a1-2)
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: motion — the genus of the phantasia-definition (kinesis hypo tes aistheseos kat' energeian gignomenes)

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: Aristotle's term for the soul-power producing inner appearances; Caston standardly refuses to translate but treats explicitly as 'imagination' for thematic purposes (the title itself)
gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: Frede preserves the Greek; settles on 'appearance' as the central meaning covering capacity, activity, product; sometimes 'imagination' for the active/creative sense
gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: Central term. González argues phantasia in Rhet. III.1 1404a11 is the same psychological faculty described in De Anima — mediating between αἴσθησις and the higher cognitive faculties (ὑπόληψις, doxa, νοῦς, βούλευσις). NOT 'mere outward show.' Operative definition at Rhet. 1370a28-30: αἴσθησίς τις ἀσθενής, connected with memory and hope.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: Visual faculty; for Hawhee a fuzzy, distance-related, judgment-feeding capacity; not aisthēsis; central faculty for rhetorical vision.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: The faculty in virtue of which an animal sees an object as an object of a certain sort. Not (primarily) image-having.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-05: Central term. Word appears only nine times in the Rhetoric but pervasive via cognates. In DA: a movement of the psyche produced by sense-perception, dependent on sight; in Rhet.: the operation by which lexis affects audiences. O'Gorman insists on the broad 'appearances'-sense over the narrow 'image' or 'mere outward show'.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: the soul-power producing inner appearances; Papachristou prefers to leave untranslated (fn. 32) since 'imagination' fails to convey Aristotle's notion adequately
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: the soul-power producing inner appearances; left untranslated by White

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: the inner appearance produced by phantasia; for Caston the central object of analysis — individuated by causal powers, not causal ancestors
gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: DA 431a14: phantasmata 'serve as perceptions' to the rational soul; like sense-perceptions but without (sensible) matter
gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: The product of phantasia. DA 431a14-15: τὰ φαντάσματα οἷον αἰσθήματα ὑπάρχει for the διανοητικὴ ψυχή. The orator constructs phantasmata that become the listeners' phantasia.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: Image presented by phantasia; the 'pleionōn phantasmatōn' of DA 3.11 are combined in deliberative phantasia.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Verbal noun of phainesthai. 'What appears.' Sometimes image, but not by lexical necessity.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-05: The product of phantasia. DA 432a: 'like aisthemata, only without matter.' Rhet. operates through the production of corporate phantasmata via lexis.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: the products of phantasia — appears 12 times in DA; Papachristou translates differently in two registers: 'representation/image' (when phantasma relates only to phantasia) vs. 'mental representation/mental image' (when substratum on which mind works)
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: the inner appearance produced by phantasia; in Aristotle restricted to interior reflections (unlike Plato, who uses it for outer reflections)

greek_script_attestations: δυνάμει νοῦς / ἐνεργείᾳ νοῦς / ἐντελεχείᾳ νοῦς

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: actuality / actively-operating; the key qualifier in the definition κίνησιν ὑπὸ τῆς ἐνεργείας τῆς αἰσθήσεως
gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: phantasia is kinesis hypo tes aistheseos tes kat' energeian — by active operation of perception
gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: De motu causal chain features phantasia as KINETIC mediator. Not González's focus terminologically but conceptually load-bearing.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: Activity, actuality; in style, 'signify things engaged in activity' (Rhet. 3.11.1411b.22-23); 'presence of the thing' (Metaph. 9.5.1048a.32-34); opposed to dunamis.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-05: Rhet. III.11. The vividness of metaphor. Per Newman (2002, 20): a kind of kinēsis realized in lexis. Per n.4 (Keuls): not etymologically identical to enargeia but contaminated in rhetorical literature.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: potential mind / actuality mind / actuality-mind — the threefold ontological distinction of nous Papachristou inherits from Philoponus
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: to actualize / actualization — sensation is energein

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: sensation/sense-perception; the most basic perceptual operation; for Caston, infallibly true of proper perceptibles
gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: the faculty on which phantasia is parasitic / supervenient
gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: Phantasia mediates between aisthēsis and higher cognitive faculties. αἴσθησίς τις ἀσθενής is the operative definition. Phantasia never occurs without aisthēsis (DA 427b14-16).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: Sensation, direct perception; phantasia distinct from aisthēsis (DA 428a.5-8); paired with phantasia in 'weak perception' phrase.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Passive impress; reception of form without matter; quality-receptive, not substance-receptive.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: sensation / sensible objects / sensitive-faculty

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: the sensitive faculty/capacity — same in subject as φανταστικόν, different in being (De insomn. 1, 459a16-18)
gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: Insomn. 459a8: dreams attributed to aisthetikon qua phantastikon
gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: 'Sensory' (DA 3.11.434a.6) — 'phantasia in the form of sense.'
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: The capacity-name (vs. activity-name aisthesis); same dunamis as phantastikon under another description.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: sensitive — the second kind of phantasia (DA III.10 433b29; III.11 434a5-7); also the second faculty/power of the soul
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: sensation / sensible objects / sensitive-faculty

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: to conceive/think; Caston uses 'conceive' to distinguish from broader 'thinking' (διανοεῖσθαι)
gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: form of forms; clean slate; thinks by itself once it has grasped immaterial forms; apathes
gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: The higher cognitive faculty. Renaissance commentators articulated 'the relationship between mens (νοῦς) and animus (θυμός) on the fulcrum of phantasia.' DA 431a16-17: οὐδέποτε νοεῖ ἄνευ φαντάσματος ἡ ψυχή.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Separable from body (DA III.5); its activities require phantasia as bodily-correlated correlate.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: mind / rational-faculty / discursive-faculty — sixth faculty in Papachristou's six-fold table; in humans only
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: thinking / the power of thought, distinct from sensation; the unifying theme of DA III.3-11

gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: DA 433b29, 434a5-7: human-specific subdivision of phantasia for practical reasoning
gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: DA 434a5-10: the rational animal can ἐκ πλειόνων φαντασμάτων combine one course of action. The orator's craft activates the listeners' bouleutikē phantasia.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Rational species of phantasia (DA III.11 433b28); supports phantasia ek syllogismou.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-05: DA 434a: bouleutikē as combining many phantasmata into one. Also used in NE 1141b, Pol. 1329a, Rhet. 1383a of political-council deliberation. NE 1113a: proairesis is bouleutikē orexis. Bridges psychic phantasia to civic deliberation.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: deliberative — the second equivalent epithet (DA III.11 434a7); 'λογίζομαι' and 'βουλεύομαι' both mean 'to determine, consider'

gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: Insomn. 462a1: phantasia counterpart to doxa; assertion of universal predicate of sensible object
gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: Rhetoric is wholly πρὸς δόξαν. Survey of Rhetoric occurrences yields 'opinion/reputation' as dominant sense, not 'ostentation.' DA 428a20-24: phantasia and doxa distinct — phantasia does not necessarily carry πίστις.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Belief based on experience; contrasted with phantasia.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-05: DA 428a: phantasia produces doxa 'exactly corresponding to direct perception.' Per Fortenbaugh: doxa is the efficient cause of emotion. The doxa-phantasia-emotion circuit is what lexis mobilizes.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: judgment / forming an opinion — distinguished from phantasia by reference beyond us to truth or falsity

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: acceptance/judging-to-be-the-case; the genus of belief
gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: DA 427b27: phantasia subsumed as counterpart of hupolepsis
gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: DA 427b14-16: ὑπόληψις never occurs without phantasia. Phantasia is constitutive of the very faculty by which rhetorical kriseis are formed.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: supposition — difficult term per Hamlyn; Philoponus's gloss includes ἐπιστήμη/φρόνησις/δόξα; Hamlyn-Polansky and Hicks render 'supposition'
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: judgment / forming an opinion — distinguished from phantasia by reference beyond us to truth or falsity

gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: Broad sense: anything from πάσχειν — emotions, bodily states (sleep, memory, phantasmata). The pathē of De motu are bodily; the psychic pathē of Rhetoric II precede desire and motivate judgment. Emotions are phantasiai (Rhet. 1382a21, 1384a22).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: Emotion(s); 'seen through phantasia' (p.150); 'irreducibly visual' (Hawhee on Gross 2006).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-05: DA 427b: pathos as the kind of phantasia that lies in our power. Rhetorical emotions (phobos, aischynē) defined as phantasiai. The interface between phantasia, doxa, and rhetorical effect.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: affection — phantasia as πάθος ἐφ' ἡμῖν (in our own power, DA III.3 427b14-21)
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: affection, experience — phantasia involves the persistence of pathos beyond sensation

gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: etymological roots; Aristotle treats phantasia as the noun corresponding to phainesthai
gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: Verbal stem related to phantasia. Aristotle's φανῆναι at Rhet. 1403b17 is read as deliberate signaling of the psychology of perception. φαινόμενοι ἔλεγχοι at SE 164a20-21 names the fallacy-as-phantasia phenomenon.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: The verb that anchors the entire phantasia-family lexically.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-05: Verbal stem to which phantasia is grammatically related. Nussbaum's broadening of phantasia is via the phainesthai-stem — what appears, not just what is imaged.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: appears (3rd sg.) — the verb governing the 'appearings' that phantasia accounts for

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: the imaginative faculty/capacity
gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: the CAPACITY; DA 432a31; Aristotle expresses doubt whether it is a separate faculty (toi men einai... heteron)
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: The capacity-name for phantasia; same dunamis as aisthetikon under another description.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: the imaginative faculty (DA III.9 432a28-432b4); the part/faculty whose power produces phantasia; placed between sensation and thought
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: the imaginative faculty — same as aisthetikon but different in einai (De Ins. 1, 459a15-22)

gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: DA 433b29, 434a5-7: human-specific subdivision of phantasia for practical reasoning
gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: DA 433b29-30. The rhetorical-art works with logistikē, but via phōnē + skhēmata accesses aisthētikē in audiences (Labarrière 1984).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Alternative name for the rational species of phantasia (DA 433b29).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: calculative — one of the two equivalent epithets for the third kind of phantasia (DA III.10 433b29)

gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: DA 433b27-30: animal motion presupposes ὄρεξις, which presupposes phantasia. The De motu causal chain: thought/perception → phantasia → orexis → bodily pathē → motion.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Jointly necessary with phantasia for animal motion.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: appetitive — faculty including desire/spiritedness/wish; cause of animal movement; cannot exist without phantasia (DA III.10 433b28-29)
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: desire — paired with phantasia in passages on action (DA III.10 433a9-12 quoted in fn. 45)

gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: Verbal stem related to phantasia. Aristotle's φανῆναι at Rhet. 1403b17 is read as deliberate signaling of the psychology of perception. φαινόμενοι ἔλεγχοι at SE 164a20-21 names the fallacy-as-phantasia phenomenon.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: 'Apparent pleasures' — the rhetorically operative class of pleasures (Rhet. 1.11).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: In Aristotelian method (after Owen), the explanatory starting-points — broader than perception-data.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: the appearances; what appears

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: the initial sensory stimulation in peripheral sense-organs — distinguished from αἴσθησις (the experience in central organ); the immediate cause of the phantasma in Caston's Diagram 2
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: The form-without-matter received in aisthesis.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: the things sensed — paired with phantasmata in 431a14-15; 432a8-10

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: alteration; the broader and the technical sense matter to Caston's reconstruction of premise (6)
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: The bodily change that is the matter of aisthesis.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: alteration, change of state — used to explain persistence of pathos after sensation in De Insomniis

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: discursive thought/reasoning; can be false, unlike noein
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Listed alongside nous as a kritikon (MA 6).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: calculation / reason / discursive thinking — DA III.3 contrasts phantasia with logos-having creatures

greek_script_attestations: δυνάμει νοῦς / ἐνεργείᾳ νοῦς / ἐντελεχείᾳ νοῦς

gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Mathematical dunamis is a kata metaphoran extension (Metaph. 1019b33).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: potential mind / actuality mind / actuality-mind — the threefold ontological distinction of nous Papachristou inherits from Philoponus
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: potentially — thought potentially identical with the eide

gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: the active sense (DA 427b18-20); ruled out at 428a2 as kata metaphoran
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Common Platonic word for representational image (Rep. 601b); used in MA 702a5 for memory-as-shadow.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: phantoms, images, reflections — phantasmata likened to eidola in water (De Prophetia in Somno 2, 464b9)

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: to be / in being; the formula for distinguishing always-coinstantiated powers (DA 3.9, 432a31-b1; De insomn. 1, 459a16-18)
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: In 'different in einai' formula: same capacity under different descriptions.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: being, essence — the einai of sensible things which nous extracts from phantasmata; phantasia and aisthesis 'same but different in einai'

gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: DA 426b8-14: aisthesis as critical/judgmental faculty
gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: Rhetoric is ἕνεκα κρίσεως (Rhet. 1377b20-22). Phantasia is a κριτικόν faculty (De motu an. 700b17-21) — occupies the same place as νοῦς in soul-mapping.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-05: Rhet. 1358b: deliberative/judicial audiences are kritai. Krisis as end of rhetoric (Rhet. 1358b). Phantasia conditions krisis because lexis-produced phantasmata mediate audience judgment.

gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: The subject of Rhetoric III. González reads lexis at 1404a11 broadly: τὸ περὶ τὴν λέξιν includes hypokrisis as a subordinate division. Lexis is the rhetorical medium that produces phantasmata.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: Style, diction; the matter of Rhet. III; the medium through which rhetors tap phantasia.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-05: The subject of Rhetoric III; conjoined with phantasia at 1404a. Lexis is 'artistic' (entechnon) and thus dangerous (Rhet. 1354a); it produces visual images in the auditor's psyche.

translation_pool: by transference; in a transferred sense

gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: Metaphor; in Rhet. 3.2 and 3.10-11 the chief carrier of energeia and bringing-before-the-eyes.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Aristotle's standard marker for non-literal extension. Used at DA 428a4 — Nussbaum rereads to bracket the 'mere show' sense.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: in a transferred sense — at DA 428a1 (preceding kath' hen formula); White brackets transferred uses to focus on subjective sense

translation_pool: to appear; to imagine; to be presented with

gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: etymological roots; Aristotle treats phantasia as the noun corresponding to phainesthai
gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: Verbal cognate. Hdt. 7.10ε is the sole pre-Aristotelian candidate for 'arrogant display' coloring — González: strictly contextual, not lexicalized.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Verb cognate; in Hdt./Polybius acquires 'make a show' sense.

gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: Light; the (dubious) etymological root Aristotle gives for phantasia at DA 429a.4-5; Demosthenes' light/dark imagery (Funeral Speech 24).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-05: DA 429a etymology: phantasia derived from phaos because 'without light it is impossible to see.' Emphanizōn (1367b) and dēloi (1404a) form a vocabulary cluster of lexis-as-illumination.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: light; Aristotle's derivation-source for phantasia at DA 429a3-4

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: conviction; the differentia of belief from phantasia
gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: Rhetoric's goal is phantasia-WITH-pistis. Plural pisteis = the three rhetorical proofs (logos/ethos/pathos). Pistis attends doxa but not always phantasia (DA 428a20-24).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Required by doxa, lacking in animals (DA 428a21-23). Distinguishes doxa from phantasia.

gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: Rhet. 1386a31, 1386a33-34: speakers make the evil appear ἐγγὺς through visualizing operations. Poetics 17 1455a23: πρὸ ὀμμάτων τιθέμενον. The rhetorical phantasma-construction technique par excellence.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: 'Bringing-before-the-eyes' (Rhet. 3.10.1410b.33-35; 3.11.1411b.22-23) — the stylistic operation that signifies things engaged in activity.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-05: Rhet. 1411b. Cognate with De Memoria's tithēmi pro ommatōn (450a) and Poetics' pro ommatōn tithemenon (1455a). The signature rhetorical operation by which lexis activates audience phantasia.

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: the object of sensation; ultimate cause of αἴσθημα and (indirectly) of phantasma
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: sensation / sensible objects / sensitive-faculty

gloss_by_unit.PHX-03: background term for nous's separation from body and matter
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: unmixed (with matter and body) — the distinguishing mark of nous

gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: Amplification; aims to show hyperochē (1.9.1368a.40); home in epideictic; Hawhee links to Isocrates' auxein.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-05: Rhet. 1368a. Falls among forms of praise; shows superiority; most at home in epideictic — 'clothing actions with greatness [megethos] and beauty [kallos].' The signature operation of epideictic phantasia.

gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: What phantasia presents — the object's formal content (as F).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: forms — what nous and aisthesis receive; nous receives them amige (unmixed)

gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Likeness contrasted with phantasma (Plato Sophist 236b).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: images — phantasmata regarded as eikones of past objects in memory (De Mem. 450a25-451a14)

gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: Vividness; paired with energeia by Kennedy as 'visual-rhetorical concepts' (p.140).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-05: Latin: illustratio / evidentia. Quintilian's translation-context. Etymologically distinct from energeia but conflated with it in Greco-Roman rhetorical theory.

gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Species of desire ascribed to even incomplete creatures (DA III.11).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: desire / spiritedness / wish — the three components of the appetitive faculty (DA II.3 414b1-2; III.9 432b3-6)

gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: One of the three rhetorical proofs. González: a speaker's ethos-construction is reinterpretable as 'phantasia toward the hearers with a view to creating pathē.' Hence ethos and pathos overlap, contra Fortenbaugh 1996.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: Speaker's character; 'sutured to rhetoric' via reputation that 'heightens the seeing' (p.147).

gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: Rhetoric is ἕνεκα κρίσεως (Rhet. 1377b20-22). Phantasia is a κριτικόν faculty (De motu an. 700b17-21) — occupies the same place as νοῦς in soul-mapping.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: to distinguish / the distinguishing-power; the major Aristotelian division of soul-powers at III.9 432a15-17

gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: Rhetoric is ἕνεκα κρίσεως (Rhet. 1377b20-22). Phantasia is a κριτικόν faculty (De motu an. 700b17-21) — occupies the same place as νοῦς in soul-mapping.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: to distinguish / the distinguishing-power; the major Aristotelian division of soul-powers at III.9 432a15-17

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: reason/account; phantasia exists without logos in animals; conviction does not occur without logos
gloss_by_unit.PHX-02: calculation / reason / discursive thinking — DA III.3 contrasts phantasia with logos-having creatures

gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: Magnitude, greatness, loftiness (1.9.1368a.25-30); epideictic's task to clothe actions in megethos.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-05: Centerpiece term. Per Farrell (1995, 186) the 'root of a great many recurring issues in Aristotelian inquiry.' Tied to megaloprepeia, megalopsychia, the more/less. At the heart of amplification in epideictic; cited at Rhet. 1368a as what 'remains to clothe the actions with' once they are agreed upon.

gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: Rhet. 1370a28-30: phantasia attends memory. De Mem. 449b4-6: mnēmē as pathos.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: memory — bees have memory (Metaph. I.1 980b22-25); memory involves phantasia (De Mem. I 450a12-17)

gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: Verbal cognate. Hdt. 7.10ε is the sole pre-Aristotelian candidate for 'arrogant display' coloring — González: strictly contextual, not lexicalized.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: 'To phantasize' — Hawhee's English coinage from the verbal form.

gloss_by_unit.PHX-06: Hypokrisis ἐν τῇ φωνῇ (1403b27-28). Phōnē as σημεῖον of pleasure/pain (Pol. 1253a10-11). Bridge between αἰσθητική phantasia and rhetorical practice (Labarrière).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Living creature's sound; meaningful only via phantasia.

gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: 'Meaning-making' (DA 2.8.420b.32) — voice's distinguishing capacity, tied to phantasia.
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: DA II.8 420b32 — voice is semantikos because produced by a phantasizing creature.

gloss_by_unit.PHX-07: Picture (De Memoria); pressed-in 'kind of picture' on the soul (1.450a.27ff.).
gloss_by_unit.PHX-01: Mem. 450a30 — image qua painting; Nussbaum: metaphorical assimilation, not lexical identity.

gloss_by_unit.PHX-04: the relative-clause introducer in De insomn. 2, 460b23 — Caston's careful note in fn. 66 that this introduces a same-content phrase, not generic 'anything whatsoever'
simple things / indivisibles (DA 3.6, 430a26-27, b27-28); the objects of infallible conception

gloss_by_unit.PHX-08: inarticulate — Themistius's gloss on the phantasia of imperfect animals (5.3.122.11-12)
to perceive (by sense) — phantasia results from αἰσθάνεσθαι; sensitive phantasia generated by sense-perception (DA III.10 433b29-30)
